title: Create a minimal Python utility in ./fusion-test2: add.py
description: Create a minimal Python utility in ./fusion-test2: add.py with add(a,b) and test_add.py, README.md. Keep isolated.
summary: I'll review the worktree changes for this task. Created the isolated `fusion-test2/` utility: `add.py` provides `add(a, b)` returning the plain sum, `test_add.py` contains six assert-based test functions (positives, negative operands, zeros, decimals, zero identity) with a dependency-free runner that prints PASS/FAIL lines and exits non-zero on failure, and `README.md` documents usage, the function reference, and the test commands. The new directory touches nothing outside itself, so the existing `calculator/` package and root README are unchanged. Verification was limited to static review in this step (read-only tooling); the documented command `python3 fusion-test2/test_add.py` is self-contained and requires no third-party packages, and the README's documented `6 passed, 0 failed` output matches the six tests present.

stepReports.summary: Preflight complete: worktree has README.md, docs/, .gitignore and no fusion-test2 directory; git status is clean; python3 is 3.14.2; no package.json/pyproject.toml/setup.cfg/pytest.ini/conftest.py exists, so verification is Python-native only.
Created fusion-test2/add.py with a single typed, side-effect-free add(a, b) function using plain + and no imports. Verified via ad-hoc import check printing `5 1 3.0`; committed as 0edd8bd.

Created fusion-test2/test_add.py with six plain-assert test functions covering positive, negative, zero, decimal, both-negative, and identity-with-zero cases, plus a __main__ runner that prints PASS/FAIL per test and a `N passed, M failed` summary and exits non-zero on failure. Verified from repo root and from inside fusion-test2 (6 passed, 0 failed, exit 0); committed as 13bd5c6.

Created fusion-test2/README.md with title/description, Requirements line (Python 3 only), Usage snippet, function reference table for add(a, b), Running the tests section with both commands and the `6 passed, 0 failed` summary note, and a project layout listing. Committed as febdd78.

All Python quality gates pass: `python3 -m compileall -q fusion-test2` exit 0; `python3 fusion-test2/test_add.py` and `cd fusion-test2 && python3 test_add.py` both exit 0 with `6 passed, 0 failed` and no FAIL lines; import spot check prints `5`; failure-path proven (a mutated copy printed `5 passed, 1 failed` and exited 1, and a direct false assert exited 1) with the temporary copy removed; git status is clean with only the three fusion-test2 files tracked.

Confirmed fusion-test2/README.md matches shipped behavior (function name, signature, exact test commands, `6 passed, 0 failed` summary) and saved its full text as the task document with key "docs" (revision 1). Root README.md, docs/, and .gitignore were left untouched; three commits (0edd8bd, 13bd5c6, febdd78) carry the KB-002 prefix and the working tree is clean with only the three new files added.

findings.body: Evidence: .gitignore contains only .fusion/, .pi/, .worktrees/, fusion.db, fusion.db-wal, fusion.db-shm — no __pycache__ pattern. Step 4 runs `python3 -m compileall -q fusion-test2` and `python3 fusion-test2/test_add.py` (which imports add.py), both of which create fusion-test2/__pycache__/*.pyc. A broad `git add fusion-test2` would then stage those binaries, breaking the plan's own acceptance criteria ('git status --porcelain shows only the three new files'). Correction for the implementer: after the verification runs, delete fusion-test2/__pycache__ (or stage the three paths explicitly: `git add fusion-test2/add.py fusion-test2/test_add.py fusion-test2/README.md`), and re-check the staged file list before each commit. Do not add a .gitignore inside fusion-test2 or modify the root .gitignore, as both are out of scope.
